# hermes-on-Apple-container — live-prototype verdict (2026-07-15)

Supersedes the 2026-07-14 spike memo (note 452679f). Executes the 5-experiment matrix from backlog task 89dbaae on the live host (apple/container 1.1.0 + socktainer 1.1.1 installed with user approval). Full chronology + artifacts: cc-notes log `apple-container-prototype` (carries the verified proxy-fix diff as an attachment). Both the E1 finding AND this verdict took a gpt-5.6-sol adversarial refuter pass; challenges were verified/rejected directly (below).

**Verdict: NO-GO for immediate production. The one CONFIRMED FAIL is lifecycle/recovery (#158/#286 — no boot-autostart, no restart policy). The other gates are favorable-to-neutral but each carries a named residual risk that wasn't disqualifying on the tests run and isn't fully closed either — this is NOT "everything's fixed except lifecycle."** The prototype's value: it turned "unknown, prototype-able" into "sandbox works with one small verified proxy fix; egress isolable via custom networks; memory idle-footprint favorable; and a concrete, mostly-buildable prerequisite list." The lifecycle blocker is upstream-tracked and buildable-around, not fundamental.

## Conjunctive gate table

| Gate | Verdict | Evidence + residual |
|---|---|---|
| **Sandbox path** | ✅ **CONDITIONAL PASS (w/ fix)** | proxy→socktainer→apiserver→micro-VM: 14 routes work; 9 host-escape bodies 403'd. A CRITICAL host-escape was found + **fixed + verified** (below). Fix tested against the full path-normalization bypass surface: alternate socket names (containerd/dockerd/.bak — not relayed), parent-dir mount (relay doesn't fire), trailing-slash + `..`-traversal (both 403 via filepath.Clean). **Residual**: a full audit of socktainer's own mount-relay SOURCE code (only the empirical surface was probed). |
| **Egress isolation** | ⚠️ **PARTIAL — needs enforcement** | Fleet (metal/hermes/bb) unreachable on BOTH vmnet 192.168.64.x AND tailscale 100.x IPs; host gateway/LAN closed; IPv6 blocked. **BUT a DEFAULT-network container reaches the host's OWN tailnet services** (rapid-mlx 100.88.252.58:8000, mlx-audio :8765) + internet (NAT). A **CUSTOM non-NAT network reached NOTHING**. **Residual**: only IPv4 TCP tested; UDP / mDNS(5353) / the full machines.json port set untested. |
| **Recovery / lifecycle** | ❌ **FAIL (the blocker)** | NO component auto-restarts (apiserver #158; socktainer + proxy unsupervised). Recovery needs a KeepAlive supervision layer (the fleet's `write_agent` pattern). Cold-boot leg deferred (no-reboot constraint). Clean, well-scoped fail. |
| **Memory** | ⚠️ **INSUFFICIENT DATA (idle only)** | ~340 MB RSS per IDLE micro-VM measured (via the XPC backing process); a 2G machine holds ~356 MB idle (no pre-wiring). **The operationally decisive dimension — load/growth + the no-page-release ratchet for an always-on agent — was NOT cleanly measured** (test contaminated; deferred). No clean tart-side idle comparison either, so "favorable vs tart" is a reasoned prior, not a measured result. |
| **Backup** | ✅ **PASS** | Bind-mount host paths keep restic file-level (files appear directly on host). Named volumes are opaque ext4 images → migration MUST bind-mount hermes state. Minor untested edge: restic consistency snapshotting a live-writing named-volume image (moot if we never use named volumes). |
| *(bonus)* **Wholesale NixOS-in-a-machine** | ⚠️ **boot-blocked** | Not gate-critical (sandbox gate met by the socktainer path). Apple machine rootfs is read-only; NixOS's `/etc/resolv.conf` symlink into `/nix/store` fails Apple's `configureDns`. A scoped image-fix (writable `/etc` overlay) is in flight on hermes. |

## The critical finding (why the adversarial pass mattered)
socktainer transparently relays a container-internal `/var/run/docker.sock` **target** to its own raw, unfiltered API — regardless of mount source (relay is `docker.sock`-basename-EXACT; other names + parent-dir + trailing-slash + `..` all verified NOT to reach it under the fix). hermes-docker-proxy screened bind/mount **sources** but never **destinations**. Exploit run end-to-end THROUGH the proxy: `docker run -v <bindroot>/empty:/var/run/docker.sock` (passes source screening) → inside, that path is a live socktainer socket → `docker run --privileged -v /:/hostroot` mounted the **HOST filesystem** (read `/Users/yasyf` = sops key + vault token). Full proxy bypass → host compromise. **Fixed**: a `forbiddenDest()` destination screen (rejects any bind/mount whose `filepath.Clean`'d target basename is `docker.sock`) — 403s the exploit (`-v` and `--mount`), leaves legit binds working, existing tests green. Diff attached to the log; port task da1c63. (Not exploitable on the live dockerd proxy — dockerd has no relay — but a hard socktainer-migration prerequisite and cheap defense-in-depth now.)

## Egress — corrected detail
Cross-vmnet + cross-tailnet-peer isolation is strong: no container reached the fleet's 192.168.64.x OR their real tailscale 100.x IPs (the host doesn't forward container→tailnet-peer traffic), nor the host gateway/LAN, nor IPv6. The leak is narrow but real: a container on the **NAT'd default network** reaches the **host's own** tailnet-IP services + the open internet, because it NATs through the host. A **custom `container network create` network is NOT NAT'd and reached nothing**. Mitigation (a migration requirement): code-exec sandboxes on a **custom non-NAT network** (verified zero-egress); hermes-the-agent on a controlled network with pf/tailscale-only egress.

## Production prerequisites (conjunctive)
1. **Proxy destination-screening** (task da1c63) — REQUIRED; ready fix verified.
2. **Lifecycle supervision** — KeepAlive/boot-autostart wrapper for apiserver + socktainer + proxy + the agent machine (mirrors the tart `write_agent` stack). The one architectural build item; #158/#286 would obviate it.
3. **Egress enforcement** — sandboxes on a custom non-NAT network; hermes on a controlled network + pf/tailscale-only egress. Close the UDP/full-port coverage gap during the build.
4. **tailscale in-container** — userspace-networking (proven to start, no caps); reaches metal over the tailnet. Full join+reach-metal pending an ephemeral tag:hermes key.
5. **Bind-mount state** (never named volumes) so restic keeps working.
6. **Drop `--runtime runsc`** from the agent's docker args (socktainer ignores it; per-VM boundary replaces gVisor — stronger).
7. **Measure memory under real load** before trusting the win — the idle number is not enough for an always-on agent.
8. Optional: the wholesale-NixOS-machine path (needs the read-only-rootfs image work).

## Proven vs open
PROVEN: sandbox filtering (with fix, full path-normalization bypass surface tested), fleet + tailnet-peer + host-gateway isolation, per-VM IDLE memory footprint, restic-compatible bind-mount backup, tailscale userspace mechanism, custom-network zero-egress, subnet-collision avoidance.
OPEN (deferred; several are named residuals above, not just "not done"): memory under load + no-release quantification; cold-boot recovery; full tailnet join; UDP/full-port egress coverage; socktainer relay-source audit; pf enforcement; the wholesale-NixOS boot; the create-body field audit (VM-isolated, low risk).

## Re-evaluation triggers (standing watch — task ad1beb; log has the one-command check)
apple/container #158 (boot autostart) or #286 (restart policy) closing removes the lifecycle blocker → strong GO signal. Also: #66 Docker-API reversal, a first-party egress primitive, ballooning completion, new container/socktainer releases.
